9	#### Geography / entities

11	- **Hessel Bottom** — a wet meadow below the Ostrey Hollow hamlet; the best milk in the Hollow came from here. Seven farms had grazing/haying rights on Hessel Bottom (per r02/Effie Loomis) — but Roy Brant (r09) says **six farms**; the largest was **Emmet Brant's** (per r02) — confirmed independently by Roy Brant (r09): the Brant farm was "the largest of the six — sixty-odd acres of the meadow, and thirty-eight cows in a good year."

15	- **Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association** — organized 1889 by valley farmers at Larrow Green. By-laws drafted by **Gideon Vose**, who was elected first president in 1889 and served until 1911 (22 years — longest of any president). Gideon Vose died in 1917.
16	- **Article VII** of the by-laws — quoted in full by Effie Loomis (r02), curator Halbert Nym (r07, Item 1), and a THIRD time by Dell Rundle (r12): *"Every patron shall be paid for the milk he delivers according to the number of pounds of butter fat contained in it, ascertained by test, and not according to the weight of the milk; and the test of the station where he delivers shall govern."* Key point emphasized by Loomis and again by Rundle: "the test of the station where he delivers shall govern" — no appeal from the station's own test, "the sentence on which the whole trouble at the head of the valley afterward turned" (Rundle). Adoption date: r02/r07 say **1892** ("adopted at the annual meeting," the year after the creamery opened); CONFLICT (r12/Rundle): states "Article VII dates from 1891, the year the churn was set up" — a one-year discrepancy against every prior source. Attorney Alonzo Frick's 1946 recollections (r13) also describe the "no appeal" rule as central and calls the whole affair "not litigation at all... an arbitration under the by-laws of a creamery association, with no appeal from it, no reported decision, and nothing whatever to cite it for."
